speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: An “estate agent” is a person or business entity that does estate agency work, and is commonly known as the estate agency or property agency.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: A “salesperson” is, among other things, an individual who, in the course of the individual’s employment or engagement by an estate agent, does estate agency work, and is commonly known as a property agent.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The real estate agency industry plays an important role in facilitating property transactions in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Buying or selling property is a major decision for many Singaporeans, and is one of the single largest investments that they will make.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Therefore, it is important that they receive the best advice before making such a transaction.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Many Singaporeans rely on estate agents and salespersons for property-related advice.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: It is essential that they do their work professionally and ethically and give their clients accurate advice that is in their clients’ best interest.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: With this in mind, the Estate Agents Act was enacted in 2010, to better protect consumer interest and raise the professionalism of the real estate agency industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: All estate agents must be licensed and all salespersons must be registered with the CEA.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In addition, estate agents and salespersons have statutory duties to ensure professional and ethical practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: To ensure compliance, CEA has investigative powers and disciplinary levers to identify and punish errant estate agents and salespersons.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: CEA also has powers to take prosecution action in Court for criminal offences under the Estate Agents Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Each salesperson must be registered through a licensed estate agent, who is primarily responsible and accountable for the supervision and management of the salesperson.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Public education is a key part of CEA’s work.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: A public register was set up to allow the public to access information about their estate agents and salespersons before engaging their services, including records of any offences committed and disciplinary penalties.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In particular, the number of complaints which led to prosecution or disciplinary action, has also dropped.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These stronger levers will ensure that estate agents and salespersons conduct their business professionally and ethically, so that we can protect the interest of consumers.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: First, the Bill gives effect to the Financial Action Taskforce (FATF) Recommendations on the preventive measures in the real estate agency industry to strengthen Singapore’s levers against money laundering and terrorism financing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: FATF is an inter-Governmental body established in 1989 to set out national and international standards to promote the effective implementation of measures to combat money laundering and terrorism financing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The FATF Recommendations form part of the broader international financial sector standards.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: They are recognised and used by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank in their assessment of a country’s financial sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Since 1992, Singapore has been a member of FATF and has put in place a very strong legislative and regulatory framework to detect, deter and take action against money laundering and terrorism financing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Singapore has committed to periodic peer assessments to ensure compliance with FATF Recommendations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This Bill continues our on-going efforts to combat money laundering and terrorism financing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The use of real estate to launder large amounts of illegal funds is a known method for money laundering.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: It opens Singapore’s non-financial and financial sectors to criminal abuse.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Safeguards are essential to detect illegal sources of funding for properties early, so that such transactions can be identified and blocked upstream.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: As intermediaries of property transactions, estate agents and salespersons have a part to play to counter these threats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: FATF has identified the real estate agency sector as crucial gatekeepers against money laundering and terrorism financing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: One example of money laundering occurred in 2016, where the Singapore Police Force (SPF) seized more than $27 million in criminal proceeds from one of China’s biggest Ponzi schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The monies were transferred to Singapore to purchase a $23.8 million Sentosa Cove bungalow, with the purchase falling through when one of the Ponzi scheme’s key accomplices was arrested in China.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: While investigations did not reveal any local parties being involved, SPF successfully prosecuted the real estate salesperson and conveyancing lawyer involved in the planned property purchase.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Both of them knew that their client, the bungalow buyer, had been arrested in China for involvement in the Ponzi schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: But, clearly, both did not fulfil their obligations to lodge Suspicious Transaction Reports with SPF.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Currently, under CEA’s practice guidelines, estate agents and salespersons are required to fulfil specific duties to counter potential money laundering and terrorism financing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Failure to comply with CEA’s guidelines may result in disciplinary action under the Estate Agents Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, FATF Recommendations require such duties and the penalties for non-compliance to be provided in "any legislation approved through a Parliamentary process".

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The FATF interprets this to mean that the duties must be set out in primary legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: First, the new sections 44A to 44D of the new Part IVA set out the duties of estate agents and salespersons on prevention of money laundering and terrorism financing in the Estate Agents Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: It requires them to conduct customer due diligence checks and report any suspicious transactions to SPF’s Suspicious Transaction Reporting Office (STRO).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For estate agents, they must also keep records of the due diligence checks that are conducted, which CEA may inspect.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Details of the duties will be prescribed in subsidiary legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Second, the new section 44E of the new Part IVA will provide that disciplinary action can be taken for non-compliance of the requirements under Part IVA.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: I will elaborate more on CEA’s disciplinary levers in the second area of the Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: To be clear, these duties are not new to the real estate agency industry and are already provided for under the CEA’s practice guidelines today.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Disciplinary action can also be taken against estate agents and salespersons who do not comply with these practice guidelines.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The Bill takes the relevant obligations to counter money laundering and financing of terrorism from the practice guidelines, and inserts them as express provisions in the Act, in order to comply with FATF Recommendations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Currently, CEA has two disciplinary levers to punish errant estate agents and salespersons.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: First, CEA can refer the case to a Disciplinary Committee, nominated from CEA’s Disciplinary Panel comprising practising solicitors, academics, professionals from the real estate industry as well as members from other professions.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The Disciplinary Committee has the power to impose a financial penalty and revoke, suspend or impose conditions on an estate agent’s licence or a salesperson’s registration.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The proceedings before a Disciplinary Committee can be a resource-intensive process.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: So, CEA generally refers more serious cases, such as cases which involve dishonesty or financial losses to the client, to the Disciplinary Committee.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The second disciplinary lever for CEA is to issue a “letter of advice”.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, this has limited deterrent and punitive effect as the fact that a “letter of advice” has been issued cannot be published in CEA’s public register under the Estate Agents Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The letter of advice also does not provide for an accompanying penalty.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Hence, the Bill will amend the Act to provide CEA with more options to deal with errant estate agents and salespersons without having to refer cases to the Disciplinary Committee.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This provides better deterrence against repeated and less serious breaches that do not warrant action by the Disciplinary Committee, but are serious enough to merit punishment.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: As a safeguard, CEA will have to first give notice of its intent to censure or issue a financial penalty, and allow the estate agent or salesperson to make representations before deciding on the penalty to impose.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Overall, the new powers to censure and impose a financial penalty provide more calibrated levers against errant estate agents and salespersons.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: A tiered structure distinguishing the maximum financial penalty for estate agents and salespersons is not unique, and can be found in other regimes that regulate professions such as accountancy, where different limits apply to the accountants and the accounting corporations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: All cases undergo a disciplinary process, where both CEA and the respondent have the opportunity to present their case to the Disciplinary Committee, before the Disciplinary Committee decides on the penalty.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For estate agents, the new maximum financial penalty of $200,000 per case will better match the higher commissions estate agents can potentially earn, compared to the individual salespersons.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The higher financial penalty limit will therefore give the Disciplinary Committee more flexibility to impose adequate punishment on estate agents, depending on the facts of each case.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: It will strengthen the deterrence against serious breaches.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The Estate Agents Act provides CEA with powers to investigate disciplinary breaches, and additional powers to investigate criminal offences, such as acting as a salesperson without being registered, and holding property transaction monies.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: To better enable CEA to identify and take action against disciplinary breaches and criminal offences, clauses 9, 10 and 17 of the Bill amend the Act to clarify and enhance CEA’s investigative powers on two fronts.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: First, clause 10 will repeal sections 46, 47 and 48 of the Act and re-enact sections 46 and 47 to clarify and enhance CEA’s powers to collect evidence in investigations under the Act, including investigations into disciplinary breaches.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Under the re-enacted section 46, CEA inspectors may, among other things, require any person to attend before an inspector, give statements, and provide documents to be inspected, copied or extracted.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This is for the purpose of ascertaining whether the Act has been or is being complied with or for the purposes of any investigations under the Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Clause 17 amends section 64 of the Act to make it an offence if the person, without reasonable excuse, does not comply with such requirements, or provides false or misleading information.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These changes will better enable CEA to obtain the necessary evidence from salespersons, estate agents and witnesses for disciplinary breaches.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Second, in view of technology adoption in the industry, the Bill will allow CEA inspectors to require any person to provide, among other things, any document, computer or computer output to be inspected, copied or extracted.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This is for the purpose of ascertaining whether the Act has been or is being complied with or any investigation under the Act, whether of disciplinary breaches or criminal offences.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Clause 9 inserts a new section 44F in the Act to define, among other terms, the terms “computer”, “computer output” and “document”. “Computers” include electronic devices, and “computer output” and “document” include the content and output from such electronic devices, such as WhatsApp chat logs or emails.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Clause 10 repeals and re-enacts section 46 to allow CEA inspectors to specify the form and manner in which, among other things, information, document, computer or computer output is to be provided to the inspector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This will also allow inspections to be conducted electronically or at premises under CEA’s control, instead of only at the estate agent’s premises.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The re-enacted sections 46 and 47 provide that, in the investigation of disciplinary breaches, CEA inspectors may take possession of any document, computer, computer programme, computer software or computer output when they enter into the premise of an estate agent, if certain criteria are satisfied.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For the investigation of criminal offences, CEA inspectors may exercise similar powers in any premise, whether or not in the possession or control of an estate agent.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: As a safeguard, the Bill will provide that these powers of taking possession in the re-enacted sections 46 and 47 will only be allowed under specific conditions, namely: Where the inspection, copying of or extraction of content from the document or electronic device cannot be performed reasonably without taking possession; Where the document, electronic device or its content may be interfered with or destroyed; or Where the document, electronic device or its content are required as evidence for proceedings under the Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These enhancements to CEA’s investigative powers will better enable CEA to identify and take action against errant estate agent and salespersons.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Clause 6 amends section 36 to, among other things, make it clear that CEA can publish the transaction records.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Clause 3 amends section 15 to provide, among other things, that where information is supplied to the public pursuant to any written law, including these published transaction records, CEA is protected from liability for any loss or damage suffered by any member of the public if the supply of the information is made in good faith, with reasonable care and in the ordinary course of the discharge of the duties of CEA.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Clause 18 amends section 70 to allow service of documents by electronic means, including email, to bring convenience to both the industry and CEA.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: And this will also update the Act in view of technology adoption and enhance CEA’s operational efficiency.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Clauses 2, 4 and 19 amend provisions of the Act to allow CEA to accredit Continuing Professional Development (CPD) courses.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The rationale for this change is for CEA to ensure the courses meet CEA’s guidelines.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: It also better enables CEA to protect consumer interest, punish errant estate agents and salespersons, and operate more efficiently.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: CEA conducted industry consultation on the key changes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The amendments are largely targeted at CEA’s enforcement against errant estate agents and salespersons.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For the majority of the real estate agency industry, who have been following the requirements and providing ethical and professional services to their clients, we thank you for your cooperation and efforts.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Despite attempts to cut out the middle man through websites, apps and direct sale on social media, the demand for estate agents remains high.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This proves the need for professional, ethical estate agents who deliver their services while looking out for the needs of their consumers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Since the Council for Estate Agencies (CEA) was established in 2010 to handle complaints against errant estate agents, the complaints have in fact fallen over the years.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The number has been somewhat stable in the past five years, but we should not rest on our laurels, and I appreciate the Government’s effort to bring this number down.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We have to bear in mind that these reports may not even include others who may be less knowledgeable about their entitlements and how to make a report.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Elderly selling their properties to right-size under the Silver Housing Scheme, or foreigners renting property, come to mind.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The incident came to light only because the client decided to contact the seller directly.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: No official complaint was lodged, but I learned about it from a Singaporean whose family lives in an HDB flat and has been moving house a couple of times.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Back when the elderly couple lived together with their eldest son who was unmarried, they wanted to move out from their first BTO flat to a larger house.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Their property agent had suggested they register the new house under their son’s name so they could avoid paying the Resale Levy.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: A couple of years later, the son got married, wanted to move out and get his own house, so the ownership had to be transferred.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The levy not only had to be repaid, but with interest.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: On top of that, the son now has one subsidised BTO flat under his name.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The agent did not have selfish intentions, but due to his inadequate advice, his clients incurred a financial loss.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And the mistake would follow them for the rest of their lives.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some real estate agents place their self-interests far above their clients’.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Others observe the ethics but lack the knowledge and empathy to engage and understand the layman consumers, which results in costly mistakes.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The HDB laws can be complex to some to ensure public housing remains affordable and grants stay relevant to the various demographics, while preventing people from profiteering from these subsidies.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Therefore, due to the complexities of the policies, there can be a certain amount of confusion when it comes to transactions.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: That is why it is important to have estate agents who are knowledgeable about the policies and capable of helping their consumers understand them.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To further enhance the standards of the real estate industry, I hope more training and courses can be made available to estate agents to hone their communication skills, keep their knowledge up to date and reinforce information about the laws and ethics to abide by.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think that this will help to reduce the amount of dissatisfaction towards the industry, especially in cases where unprofessional conduct was not intentional.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I note that real estate agents can benefit from the SkillsFuture Study Award for the real estate agency industry.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But how many are attending such courses, and are the courses truly relevant and specific to their services?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I also note that some large real estate agencies do provide opportunities for their agents to upskill themselves, but not all do so.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, I hope the Government can encourage more agents to upskill themselves through SkillsFuture and to meet CEA's guidelines.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Indeed, real estate agencies need to take greater responsibility for the professionalism of their agents and the industry as a whole.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With the new regulations, are agencies capable of assessing the compliance and duties, as well as the code of conduct of their estate agents, as Minister of State Mr Zaqy mentioned earlier?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: There may be a need for them to beef up or set up compliance units.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What role do real estate agencies play in investigations and disciplinary actions against errant agents registered under their agencies?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think the consumers should be able to go to agencies to seek help and give their feedback on errant real estate agents.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This may help to filter out cases involving misconduct, from unprofessionalism and poor service.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Of course, this should not be done at the expense of consumers having to wait longer.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Property transactions incur huge amounts of money and, certainly, it is something to watch out for over concerns of money laundering and financing of terrorism.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The high property prices made it possible for millions to be moved across borders, especially when it involves the purchase of buildings, factories and others.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If not, how does it differ from MAS guidelines on Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT)?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Private properties and land attract significant amounts of foreign investment.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Meanwhile, property transactions often play out as milestones and significant developments in the lives of a typical Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For example, when one is thinking of expanding their family, moving nearer to schools or workplaces, having ageing parents move back with them to facilitate better care, or, in the case of retirees, to right-size their homes so that they can live more comfortably and so on.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, I have a few questions and clarifications for the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Property agents play an important role in the home ownership journeys of many Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This will, hopefully, serve as an effective deterrent against unethical and unprofessional conduct.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The proposed increase in financial penalties is also timely, as 2019 saw a number of high-profile cases of agent misconduct publicised in the news.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Additionally, having the demerit points system made public would also serve as a simple, yet effective deterrent against the commission of such breaches.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In addition to fulfilling our obligations as a member of the Financial Action Task Force, the framework will also remind all property agents of their duties to perform the necessary due diligence checks.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, I note, as the Minister of State mentioned in his speech, that the proposed anti-money laundering and anti-terror financing requirements are already covered under existing CEA regulations and Practice Guidelines.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, just to be clear, can the Minister of State confirm that the proposed framework will not result in any material change to the way due diligence and suspicious transactions reporting need to be conducted henceforth?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Some, especially the younger agents, have been able to adapt and embrace technology to reach out to prospective clients virtually.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With digital literacy and digital marketing skills increasingly viewed as critical core skills, could the Ministry consider reviewing the Continuing Professional Development (CPD) Framework and list these digital skills as Professional Competencies?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Lastly, considering the impact of COVID-19 on the industry, I would like to ask the Ministry to consider waiving licence renewal fees for all estate agents and registered salespersons for the next renewal cycle.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This will help in some small way to support the profession at this very difficult time.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The proposed amendments in the Bill will empower the CEA to keep up with evolving industry practices and help deter errant and unethical behaviour by rogue property agents.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This would better protect both property buyers and property sellers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: First, there were several questions about the duties related to the prevention of money laundering and terrorism financing.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are duties aligned with the international standards set by the Financial Action Task Force or FATF, and are the key building blocks for an effective regime to prevent money laundering and terrorism financing.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This standard applies to various sectors, including estate agents, lawyers and the financial sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked how the duties under the Bill compare to those for the financial sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have taken a risk-based approach and calibrated the specific requirements for the real estate agency industry vis-a-vis other industries.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, salespersons are required to conduct customer due diligence checks when facilitating a sale or purchase of a property.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For banks, there are instances where additional due diligence checks are required, such as when conducting a wire transfer transaction of more than $1,500, which are not relevant to estate agents and salespersons in this case.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat also asked whether estate agents are capable of assessing the compliance of their salespersons with the duties under the Bill.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Estate agents and salespersons are already required to fulfil duties to counter money laundering and terrorism financing.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Disciplinary action can be taken for the failure to perform these duties today.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Bill merely inserts express provisions on these duties in the Act, in order to comply with FATF Recommendations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Hence, the industry is familiar with the duties and has already been performing them.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To facilitate compliance, CEA has consulted with the industry to put in place guidelines to provide clarity on the steps and checks required to comply with the duties.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This includes checklists to guide salespersons and estate agents on the conduct of customer due diligence checks and to determine if there is suspicion of money laundering or terrorism financing.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, where there are complex or unusually high-value transactions, salespersons should ask clients about the purpose of the transaction and the clients' source of funds.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are some of the red flags to assess if the transaction was meant to launder monies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Salespersons should also look out for suspicious indicators of money laundering or terrorism financing, such as adverse news concerning the client, paying a substantial downpayment in cash or paying a higher price for a property without viewing.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Next, on investigations of estate agents and salespersons, Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about the role estate agents play in investigating customer complaints and disciplining errant salespersons, as well as the average time taken for the industry to resolve consumer complaints.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: CEA has a framework to assess and classify complaints and works together with estate agents to address these complaints.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Estate agents are required to manage and supervise their salespersons.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And where there are non-compliances, they need to take the necessary remedial actions to prevent a repeat of a similar incident.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For service-related complaints, such as being late for appointments or unsatisfactory services, CEA will refer them to the estate agent to resolve the matter.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Similarly, for complaints involving minor disciplinary breaches, such as advertisements with a missing salesperson's registration number, or making claims on a salesperson's area of expertise in advertisements that cannot be substantiated, CEA will refer the complaint to the estate agent for them to take the appropriate action against the errant salesperson.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These typically conclude within three months as well.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For complaints involving more serious disciplinary breaches and criminal offences under the Act, CEA takes between six and 12 months to complete its investigation, depending on the nature and complexity of its cases.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Those which proceed to Court or Disciplinary Committee hearings may take several months to complete the proceedings.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, this will allow CEA to deal with these cases more efficiently, hopefully quicker for all concerned.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked about the number of complaints in 2019 and how many agents have been sanctioned by CEA.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In total, six cases were prosecuted in Court, five of which resulted in fines being imposed.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Seventeen cases were concluded by the Disciplinary Committee where disciplinary action was taken and CEA issued 206 Letters of Advice to errant estate agents and salespersons.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Member also suggested to introduce a demerit points system as a simple and effective way to deter first-time minor breaches, so that such breaches would not result in a censure or financial penalty.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: CEA will take into consideration the severity of the breach and whether the estate agent or salesperson is a repeat offender.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, for minor breaches, CEA will generally refer the matter to the estate agent for them to take the appropriate action or CEA may issue a warning letter.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If the minor breaches are repeated, then CEA may issue a letter of censure.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If the salesperson commits yet another minor breach, CEA may consider imposing financial penalties as a stronger deterrent.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Hence, first-time minor breaches will not result in a censure or financial penalty.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In a way, this incremental approach works like a demerit points system and these disciplinary actions will also be published on the CEA Public Register as a strong deterrent to would-be wrongdoers in the industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On training, Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about training efforts to enhance the professional standards of the industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I agree with the Member that training is crucial to ensure that our salespersons continue to have the necessary knowledge and skills to comply with regulations and safeguard consumer interest.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is why Continuous Professional Development (CPD) training is a key component of CEA's regulatory framework.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: CEA recently reviewed its CPD framework last year to place emphasis on both Professional and Generic Competencies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The courses on Professional Competencies ensure salespersons are competent and have updated knowledge of relevant laws and regulations, property markets as well as policies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the other hand, courses on Generic Competencies cover general skills relevant to the real estate agency industry, such as leadership, digital literacy and communication.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are in line with Singapore's Skills Framework list of generic skills and competencies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Both Professional and Generic Competencies are important to ensure that our salespersons have the skillsets and critical competencies to carry out their duties effectively.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Salespersons are required to complete courses from both Professional and Generic Competencies under CEA's CPD framework.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will continue to encourage that industry to upskill themselves with digital skills to enhance their service offerings.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about the SkillsFuture Study Award for the real estate agency industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The award was given to its first recipient last year and CEA will continue to offer the award to encourage more salespersons to better serve their clients.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For many salespersons today, we also have other schemes that are available to them, such as the Self-Employed Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) which NTUC manages, the Temporary Relief Fund (TRF) as well as the Self-Employed Persons (SEPs) Training Support Scheme, which enables our salespersons to also undertake courses and still get allowance while doing so.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But at the same time, I would like to also take the opportunity to commend the efforts of some of our estate agents by implementing their own resilience packages to help their salespersons.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Some property agencies have stepped up during this difficult period by extending financial help, by allowing salespersons to apply for early release of commissions; some have subsidised registered salespersons' CPD course fees; some have provided discounts on rentals by salespersons, such as training rooms and offices at the estate agent's premises.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think all these measures today have helped and I hope that the industry will prosper beyond this COVID-19 circuit breaker period.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It also strengthens CEA's disciplinary and investigative powers under the Estate Agents Act.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Overall, the amendments will help to deter and punish errant estate agents and salespersons to safeguard the interest of consumers and the professional reputation of the majority in the sector who discharge their duties responsibly and with care.
